clue.text: Luxurious pub I found in town's knocked over

indicators.note: pub and I are found inside the other piece, so they are placed within it
something knocked over is upended, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a city is a town, and the possessive 's is kept as a letter
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone notices a drinker in a town where things have been toppled, and calls the scene decadent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reads as an accident in the town; it reverses the town's letters to give SYTIC, which 'found in' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sybarites of ancient Sybaris were famed for pleasure-seeking, so sybaritic describes self-indulgent ease and comfort.

clue.text: Demon beginning to corrupt youth in America, bouncing up and down

indicators.note: the first letter and youth sit inside the two copies of America
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
America read downwards again gives the plain abbreviation once more

indicators.note: the beginning of the word corrupt is its first letter

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, as in a cub reporter or Cub Scout

explanation.surface: A devil sets out to deprave American youngsters, who are jumping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncing up and down' uses America twice: once read upwards, as a down clue allows, then once read normally downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A succubus is a female demon of folklore said to visit sleeping men.

clue.text: Participant in old war that's throttled by fighter

indicators.note: the soldier's throat is gripped, so another piece sits in his middle

parts.note: a Boer fought in the Boer War against the British
X means by, as in measurements such as three by four

explanation.surface: A veteran of a long-ago war is strangled by a combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is X, the multiplication sign read as 'by'. The old war also suggests the Boxer Rebellion, a neat bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer fights in the ring, so it is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Enquiry forced changes around a broadcasting channel

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the a
the letters of enquiry forced are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A demanded inquiry brings changes at a TV or radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ENQUIRY FORCED; 'around' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast signal is carried on a particular radio frequency, which is the channel a station uses.

clue.text: Country is one investing in fish

indicators.note: to invest is to cover or clothe, so the fish is clothing the other letters

parts.note: tuna is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A financial tip: some nation is putting its money into fisheries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' reads as finance, but to invest is also to clothe or surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Dreadful to-do in vehicle, giving pet access

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: a dreadful version of the word is mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A terrible fuss breaks out in a car, letting the animal in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges the fuss into TDOO; 'giving' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat flap in a door lets a household animal come and go freely.

clue.text: Very funny person, last to come to the fore in small group

indicators.text: last to come to the fore
indicators.note: the final letter of the word is brought to the front

parts.note: someone hilarious is called a riot

explanation.surface: In a little band, the comedian who came last moves to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to come to the fore' takes the T of RIOT to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, a small ensemble of performers.

clue.text: Again rouses prominent scientists to host a late party in small space

indicators.note: the scientists' letters hold the rest, as a host holds guests

parts.note: RS is the Royal Society, Britain's academy of leading scientists

indicators.note: a and the party go inside the small space

parts.note: an en is a narrow printing space
a wake is a gathering held for someone who has died, the late

explanation.surface: Eminent scientists stir again, throwing a late-night bash in a cramped room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' hints at the hour but means the dead: a wake is held for the late. The Royal Society is Britain's national science academy.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawaken is to wake again, so it means stirs someone up once more.

clue.text: Individual keeping place within the same set-up?

indicators.note: the individual keeps the other word inside

parts.note: one is a single individual
to sit something somewhere is to place it there

explanation.surface: A lone person holds a position inside an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun but is the verb 'sit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on-site happens at the same location or premises rather than elsewhere.

clue.text: Game to catch married woman cuddling German

parts.note: to contract an illness is to catch it

indicators.note: the woman holds the other letter inside, as in a cuddle

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married

explanation.surface: A scheme to snare a wife who is embracing a German man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' reads as entrap, but it means to contract a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard form of the card game bridge.

clue.text: Directed mark of error to be placed in dictionary

indicators.note: the mark is put inside the dictionary's letters

parts.note: COED is the Concise Oxford English Dictionary
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Instructions to insert a correction symbol in a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, a coxed boat is one steered by a cox, which is why 'Directed' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxswain steers a rowing boat, so a coxed crew has been steered by one.

clue.text: Having been trounced, alas, not in major papers

indicators.note: the letters, thoroughly beaten up, end in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone laments being thrashed and left out of the big newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having been trounced' rearranges ALAS NOT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: National newspapers circulate across the whole country, the big titles, as opposed to local ones.

clue.text: Pulls out expert in beer, mostly after setback

indicators.note: the expert goes inside the beer's letters
set back means turned backwards, so the word is reversed
most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: A beer connoisseur withdraws after a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the beer to STOU and 'after setback' turns that into UOTS, so the expert sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot is to tear a plant out of the ground, so the verb means extracts.

clue.text: Not breaking oven in readiness for breakfast?

indicators.note: the word is broken into a new letter order

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: the oven is working, all set for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges NOT to ONT. The question mark flags that the definition is only an example: plenty of breakfast foods are served this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs, beans and mushrooms are commonly served on toast as a morning dish.

clue.text: Aviation feature where you'd expect lowering standards

definitions.text: Aviation feature where you'd expect lowering standards

parts.words: Aviation feature where you'd expect lowering standards
parts.note: a plane's wheels are lowered before landing; read whimsically, poor deportment would be carriage that is beneath par

explanation.walkthrough: Carriage can mean deportment, so a standard of bearing that has dropped would be beneath good carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's wheels and struts, lowered for landing, form its landing gear.

clue.text: Insect to persist with cunning

parts.note: to drag on is to persist tediously
fly is slang for sharp and cunning

explanation.surface: A bug that keeps on going, and is crafty with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' as an adjective for shrewd is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a large, long-bodied flying bug of ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Shame and tears for executioner

indicators.note: read as the verb, tears rips the letters apart and rearranges them

explanation.surface: Disgrace and weeping await the hangman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like weeping but is the verb that rips SHAME AND apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsman beheaded condemned prisoners with an axe.

clue.text: A group penning paper linked to data transmission? I'll need time to get it

definitions.text: I'll need time to get it

indicators.note: the group encloses the other letters, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: a caste is a social class or group
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
DT is an abbreviation for data transmission

explanation.surface: A clique wrote a technical paper on data transfer; the reader says it will take time to grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the thing itself, something one comes to like only slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquired taste is something enjoyed only after gradual exposure, not at first try.

clue.text: Brown, in fancy tins, like some coffee

indicators.note: the colour goes inside the rearranged letters
fancy describes an ornate arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Brown stuff packed in decorative tins, like certain coffees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the tins; it rearranges them into INST.
explanation.definitionFit: Instant coffee is a powder that dissolves in hot water, a type of the drink.

clue.text: Most unconventional combination of e.g. and id est

indicators.note: the letters are combined into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pedantic note that using both Latin abbreviations together is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of' rearranges EG and IDEST, the letters of the two Latin abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means avant-garde or daring, so the superlative is the most daring.

clue.text: Skimpy swimwear enthralling river crowd

indicators.note: read as holding captive, the swimwear holds the other letter

parts.note: a thong is a scanty bikini bottom

explanation.surface: Tiny bathing costumes captivate the people by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' sounds like fascinating; it means holding R inside THONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large crowd of people.

clue.text: Cleans up? Hangs around collecting nothing

indicators.note: the hanging-about word gathers the other letter inside

parts.note: to hover is to linger or hang about
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up, or perhaps just loiters, gathering nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is a vacuum cleaner brand; in Britain it is the everyday verb for vacuuming.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacuum a floor is to clean it; the question mark marks one specific way.

clue.text: Turned grey, losing heart with assessment

indicators.note: the heart of the word, its middle letters, is lost

parts.note: taken as written
rated means given an assessment or valued

explanation.surface: Someone went grey, dispirited at how they were judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned grey' reads as one phrase, but 'Turned' is the definition. 'losing heart' drops RE from GREY to make GY.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to whirl round, so gyrated means spun or turned.

clue.text: Articles about source of tenacious Greek character

indicators.note: the articles go round the other letter

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

indicators.note: a source is a beginning, so the word's first letter

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing on the origin of a stubborn Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts THE and A round T. 'character' here is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Resting from the rink will keep one at chair

indicators.note: the outer words keep the others inside

parts.note: a skater resting is off ice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A skater sitting out holds a seat at the side of the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' looks like furniture but is the verb: to chair a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To officiate is to preside over an event or meeting, much as a chairperson does.

clue.text: About to interrupt mother? Imagine

indicators.note: the word breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: dam is a mother, especially of an animal
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to cut Mum off mid-sentence, and asks us to picture it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to', but 'About' is RE and 'to interrupt' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to fancy or picture it in the mind.

clue.text: A year's retrospective following work from artist

indicators.note: the reversed letters come after the work

parts.note: go means work, function, as a machine does

indicators.note: looking back means the letters read backwards

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A twelve-month look back after a painter's oeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' suggests a gallery show, apt for a painter, but it turns A Y into YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter and printmaker.

clue.text: Historic tax collection arrangement — then it goes wrong — lawyers brought in

indicators.note: the lawyers are put inside the rearranged letters
letters that go wrong fall into a different order

parts.note: the bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: An old levy scheme fails, so lawyers are called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges THEN IT as TITHEN; 'brought in' puts BAR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval parishes stored crops paid as a tenth-part levy to the church in a large barn.
